text:
sara: Quick sync request — we need a firm decision on who is the authoritative owner of resume tokens for streaming responses in a multi-tenant edge. Current proposals split responsibility between client-managed tokens and edge-managed opaque session IDs. thoughts?

mike: leaning toward edge-managed. Clients are flaky and we already have aggressive short-lived client tokens. If edge owns resume tokens we can enforce tenant isolation and apply backoff/priority per-tenant. but complexity increases.

devon: edge-managed + signed by control-plane KMS? that avoids replay across tenants and helps audits. downside: state explosion if we persist every in-flight session.

jin: can we make them hybrid: client holds a short resume handle, edge maps that to an ephemeral resume slot in memory + tombstone in redis when evicted? handle format = opaque_client_id:slot_hash. slot entry contains tenant, model, offset_kv.

laura: hybrid sounds reasonable. need to define eviction/backoff semantics: if slot evicted, client must retry with a new request; we should provide a clear 409/Retry-After flow so apps know to fall back.

mike: agreed re 409. also want per-tenant priority and rate-limited resumptions to avoid noisy neighbors. propose token bucket per-tenant for resume attempts with shared fallback pool.

jin: sketch of metadata i'd add to handshake:
```
Resume-Meta: {
  "handle": "opaque",           // client-visible
  "slot_id": "abcd1234",      // edge ephemeral id
  "offset": 452,               // last emitted token index
  "sig": "base64(kms-sig)"   // short expiry
}
```
This lets edge verify freshness without storing full transcript.

sara: important question: if we allow resume to re-enter the request lifecycle, do we re-run routing policies (eg: cheaper model fallback) or must we pin the original route?

devon: pinning simplifies consistency: resume continues on same model variant and node pool. but loses opportunity to fallback to cheaper model. maybe allow controlled downgrade: resume can be routed to compatible model variants in same family if primary capacity is gone, with a flag in Resume-Meta indicating `allow_variant_fallback=true`.

laura: and we need idempotency semantics. resuming after a partial response could result in duplicate tool/call side effects if we retry upstream LLM. we should conservatively treat resumed streaming as potentially duplicated unless a strict idempotency token is provided by client. document that.

mike: metric and SLO concerns: add counters for resume_attempts, resume_success, resume_evicted, resume_fallback_routed. Also histogram for time_between_fail_and_resume to monitor UX.

ops-bot: New proposal snapshot created: https://redwood.local/rfcs/session-resume-hybrid-2026 (draft).

jin: one more tradeoff: persisting resume slots to redis gives durability but increases tail latency for every resume op. in-memory only is fast but fragile on process restarts. solution: write-ahead compact tombstones to redis asynchronously: on allocation we write 1 small row, then keep full state in memory. on restart we can rebuild limited resume capacity.

sara: proposal for API surface:
- client gets `Resume-Handle` header on initial streaming response when server marks it resumable.
- to resume, client sends `POST /v1/stream/resume` with header `Resume-Handle` and `Prefer: resume-allow-variant=true|false`
- responses: 200 = resumed and continue, 409 + Retry-After = slot evicted, 410 = not resumable or expired

mike: and add `X-Resume-Quota-Remaining` in responses for tenants to introspect remaining resume budget.

laura: testing plan: canary on a single region, enable for internal tenants, run fault injector (socket tear) to ensure resume flow works with tool-calls and side-effecting prompts. add eval prompts to detect duplication.

devon: corner case: long-running KV caches (LLM kv) — when resume jumps to new node, we must ensure KV state is compatible. either require cache rehydration or only allow resume to nodes with compatible KV fingerprint. add `kv-fingerprint` to Resume-Meta.

jin: example handshake header for resume attempt:
```
Resume-Attempt: handle=opaque1234;slot=abcd;offset=452;sig=...;kv=sha256:ff12;prefer_variant=false
```
Edge verifies sig, checks tenant bucket, either routes to original node or finds compatible fallback, then streams from offset.

sara: decision proposal for this thread:
1) adopt hybrid client-visible handle + edge ephemeral slot model.
2) store minimal durable tombstones in redis, full state in memory.
3) pin by default but allow `prefer_variant` to permit benign downgrades.
4) quota resume attempts per-tenant with visible headers.
5) treat resumed requests as "possible duplicate" unless explicit idempotency on payload.

mike: +1 from me. maybe add an escape hatch: emergency-global-resume-bypass for infra when region fails.

laura: +1, will write a follow-up checklist for QA and docs. includes sample client snippets and guidance for tool-call authors to add idempotency keys.

devon: i can prototype the redis tombstone + in-memory allocator this week. will post perf numbers.

sara: awesome — i'll turn this into a short RFC and ping @eng for review. thanks all :rocket:

ops-bot: RFC created: /rfc/session-resume-hybrid-2382104567 (status: draft, reviewers: eng, eng-runtime, eng-ml).
